findings.title: whatIsNotAuthored states "the ten remaining G21 CC-5 injections" - an invented case count on another row's obligation that no governing byte carries, contradicting the subject's own summary.caseCountInvented false.
findings.measurement: The subject writes "the ten remaining G21 CC-5 injections". No governing artifact states that number. g21-leftover-join.v13 obligations[3].remainingNotAuthored.dr102 lists "remaining CC-5 injections" as an uncounted phrase alongside the ten bare CC ids; g21-fixture-corpus.v7 says "remaining CC-5 injections" at four sites; g21-fixture-corpus.v8 says it at six sites and additionally lists "Does not invent remaining CC-5 injections" among its own constraints. Across every non-review artifact in the repository the phrase is uncounted. The figure "ten" occurs only inside prior review files, which are not governing bytes for a corpus's assertions.
findings.whyItIsWrong: The count is not uniquely derivable from the bytes it would have to come from. CC-5's intent reads "Length prefix 0; prefix exactly at, one over, and far over the operative bound (pre- and post-handshake bounds separately); truncated bodies; invalid UTF-8; duplicate members; unknown members; floats, negative and over-uint53 integers." Counting injection kinds without splitting by handshake phase gives eleven; counting injections with the three prefix positions split across the pre- and post-handshake bounds as the parenthesis directs gives fourteen. g21-fixture-corpus.v7 authored two, G21.cc5.length-prefix-0 and G21.cc5.prefix-one-over-prehandshake. The remainder is therefore nine, ten or twelve depending on which reading is taken and on whether the partly-authored "one over" kind is counted as discharged. "Ten" selects one reading and states it as a recorded fact. The operative bound is itself an undecided numeric window, which is precisely why the G21 lineage refuses to count this class.
findings.whyMustFix: Three independent grounds. First, the dispatch forbids inventing a case count and the subject's own summary asserts caseCountInvented false, so the clause contradicts the document's own summary flag. Second, the count is a measurement of what remains on OBL-G21-FX-AUTHORING, an obligation on DR-114 that this corpus is explicitly forbidden to touch; stating how much of another row's leftover remains is a remainder measurement the subject has no warrant to make, and it is made in the one list whose purpose is to bound this corpus's own non-authoring. Third, it understates nothing about this corpus but overstates the precision of the record, and a later G21 remasurement citing this artifact would inherit a number the G21 lineage deliberately never recorded.
findings.remedy: Replace "the ten remaining G21 CC-5 injections" with the uncounted form the G21 lineage uses - "remaining G21 CC-5 injections". The clause then says exactly what it needs to say, that this corpus authors none of them, without measuring another row's remainder.

findings.title: remainderAfterThisCorpus asserts "six classes carry unenumerated within-class quantifiers" and classCoverage omits CC-6, whose intent names "second hello in every state" - the same construction as CC-4, which the subject does mark.
findings.measurement: classCoverage attaches remainingNotAuthored to exactly six classes - CC-1, CC-2, CC-4, CC-5, CC-7, CC-9 - each with the reason "within-class universal quantifier is named and not enumerated; this witness does not exhaust the class". remainderAfterThisCorpus then states affirmatively that leftover-design of OBL-HOSTILE-GOLDENS remains "because six classes carry unenumerated within-class quantifiers". CC-6's intent in control-protocol-contract.v2, the contract the subject cites and consumes, reads in part "second hello in every state (RF-8)" and closes "pass means every attempt ends in the typed refusal plus teardown ladder, never a lower-version session". That is a within-class universal quantifier over channel states, named and not enumerated in CC-6's own text. CC-6 carries no remainingNotAuthored and is recorded as {authoredGoldenId: HG.CC-6} alone.
findings.whyItIsWrong: The set is internally inconsistent under either reading of its own criterion. CC-4, which the subject does mark, reads "injected at EVERY channel state (AWAIT-HELLO through TEARDOWN) and at every handshake step boundary" - the same quantifier over the same domain, and CC-4 even bounds the state range explicitly where CC-6 does not. If the channel-state domain counts as enumerated, CC-4 does not belong in the set; if it does not count as enumerated, CC-6 does. Either way the six-set as recorded cannot stand, and CC-6 is the stronger case of the two because its "every state" is unqualified. The four classes the subject leaves unmarked for a defensible reason are CC-3, CC-8 and CC-10, whose intents are closed enumerations followed by a typing rule rather than a domain quantifier, and CC-11, whose own text bounds the claim to "the exercised vectors and nothing more" and expressly disclaims the universal. CC-6 does not share that shape.
findings.whyMustFix: The defect runs in the direction that matters. Omitting CC-6 records a single citation witness as exhausting a class its governing intent quantifies universally, which understates the leftover-design that remains on OBL-HOSTILE-GOLDENS. The affirmative sentence in remainderAfterThisCorpus is a claim about the cited contract's text that the cited contract's text contradicts, and the per-class partition is the accounting a later corpus or leftover-join remasurement would rely on to know what is still owed. leftoverDesignRemainingOnDR127 keeps OBL-HOSTILE-GOLDENS open, so nothing is closed in error, but the partition inside it is wrong on the bytes.
findings.remedy: Add remainingNotAuthored to classCoverage.CC-6 with the same reason the other members carry, and change remainderAfterThisCorpus from "six classes" to "seven classes". Alternatively, if the author holds that a bounded channel-state range is enumerated, drop CC-4 from the set and say so - but the two classes must be treated alike.

The identical sentence was inherited from g19-fixture-corpus.v2, whose integer 2 did not collide with the .v1 tokens it disclaimed, and where the sentence was unambiguous under both a referential and a numeric reading.
advisories.whyNotShouldFix: The established grading for exactly this issue is advisory. The Stage A review of g19-fixture-corpus.v2 recorded the misplacement of these inherited guards as CLAUDE-G19FX-V1-A-1 on the reasoning that failsIf tests for a bare version token and the guards are belt-and-braces prose rather than the mechanism that makes the tokens lawful. That reasoning holds here: every .v1 token in this subject is stemmed, the sweep is clean, and the disclaimer is true under the referential reading it was written for - the .v1 in g21-fixture-corpus.v1 denotes that lineage's version, not this speaker's. Raising it as a finding would convert prose into a defect where the mechanism is sound.
advisories.note: Worth tightening on any successor that keeps version integer 1, since the guard's plain numeric reading is false there and it is the only sentence in the document whose truth depends on which reading a later reader takes.

decision.rationale: The corpus is mechanically clean - every fixture, every digest, every quotation and the warrant all verify independently, and the consume-not-copy construction is sound. It fails on two accuracy defects in its own accounting, both contradicted by the bytes it cites and both running in the direction of understating what remains. CLAUDE-ALHG-V1-M-1 states a count of another row's unauthored remainder that no governing artifact carries and that CC-5's intent does not uniquely yield. CLAUDE-ALHG-V1-M-2 records six classes as carrying unenumerated within-class quantifiers when CC-6's intent names one in the same construction as CC-4, which the subject does mark. Both are corrigible in the subject's JSON without touching a fixture byte, and a successor that fixes them would face no other objection from this review.
